ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a grid diagram where each small square has a side length of 1, a circular arc passes through lattice points $A$, $B$, $C$. The line connecting lattice points $C$ and $D$ intersects $\arc{BC}$ at point $E$. What is the length of $\arc{EC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect AE, AC, and AD, \\
$\because \angle ABC=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore AC$ is the diameter, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle AEC=90^\circ$, \\
According to the grid figure, we know: $AC=AD=\sqrt{13}$, $CD=\sqrt{26}$, \\
$\therefore AC^{2}+AD^{2}=CD^{2}=26$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ACD$ is an isosceles right-angled triangle, \\
$\therefore \angle CAD=90^\circ$, $\angle ACE=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle EAC=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ the central angle corresponding to $\overset{\frown}{EC}$ is $90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ the length of $\overset{\frown}{EC}$ is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the circumference of the circle with diameter AC, \\
That is, the length of $\overset{\frown}{EC}$ is: $\frac{1}{4}\times \pi \times \sqrt{13}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{13}\pi }{4}}$.

From the grid in the figure it can be seen that AB and BC are perpendicular to each other, so ∠ABC=90°. Reasoning: Because A, B, C are on the same circle and ∠ABC=90°, AC is the diameter of this circle. Thus for point E on the circle, there is also ∠AEC=90°. Because AC²+AD²=13+13=26=CD², and AC=AD, △ACD is an isosceles right triangle, ∠CAD=90°, and the other two acute angles are 45°. Also because E is on CD, ∠ACE=∠ACD=45°. In △AEC, ∠AEC=90°, ∠ACE=45°, therefore ∠EAC=45°. The inscribed angle ∠EAC subtended by arc EC is 45°, so the central angle corresponding to arc EC is 90°. The diameter of the circle AC=√13, and the circumference is π√13, therefore the length of arc EC is 1/4 of the circumference, namely √13π/4.
